stops.stop: Ex Congreso Nacional, the first annual message
stops.date_confidence: The text is verbatim from the Marxists Internet Archive page filed under a September 1970 date; that filing is a cataloguing artifact. The speech self-dates to the First Annual Message to the National Congress, 21 May 1971: it speaks of six months of government, of copper coming under Chilean ownership later that year, and of the April 1972 UNCTAD conference to come. He was not president in September 1970.

stops.stop: Rancagua, the Day of National Dignity
stops.date_confidence: Attested: Congress approved Law 17,450 unanimously and Allende promulgated it on 11 July 1971 as the Day of National Dignity, nationalising the Anaconda and Kennecott properties at Chuquicamata, El Salvador and El Teniente. The venue within Rancagua, plaza or stadium, was not confirmed against a transcript in this pass.

stops.stop: Palacio de La Moneda, Fidel Castro's twenty-four days
stops.date_confidence: Attested by es.wikipedia's article on the visit: 10 November to 4 December 1971, the longest visit by a foreign head of government to Chile to that date. The farewell speech acknowledging the severity of the class conflict was given at the Estadio Nacional on 2 December, not at La Moneda; this stop is the hosting locus only.

stops.stop: Santiago, the strike of the truck owners
stops.date_confidence: The strike began in the early hours of 9 October 1972 (es.wikipedia, 'Gobierno de Salvador Allende'); its length is usually given as twenty-four to twenty-six days depending on the endpoint chosen. The Cybersyn telex network's use during it is attested by en.wikipedia's Project Cybersyn article, quoting Gustavo Silva on moving resources into the city with about two hundred trucks.

stops.stop: United Nations, New York, against the corporations
stops.date_confidence: Attested: address to the United Nations General Assembly, 4 December 1972. The text is held by the Marxists Internet Archive and the speech is among the fifty preserved by the Fundacion Salvador Allende's speech archive.

stops.stop: The Kremlin, Moscow, asking for money
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The Moscow visit in December 1972, on the same journey as the United Nations address, and the disappointing outcome are carried by the general historical record and the research dossier; no primary record of the meetings was reached in this pass, and the venue within the Kremlin complex is unconfirmed.

stops.stop: Providencia, the Opsroom on Avenida Santa Maria
stops.date_confidence: The room, its design under CORFO with Stafford Beer's team, and Beer's account of Allende's response are documented in Cybersyn scholarship. The 30 December 1972 visit date could not be confirmed against any source reached. Coordinates follow es.wikipedia's 'Proyecto Synco', which places the Opsroom in a building on Avenida Santa Maria near the Philips offices, resolved by Nominatim to Avenida Santa Maria 760.

stops.stop: Santiago, the March elections
stops.date_confidence: Attested: parliamentary elections of 4 March 1973, with Unidad Popular at about 44 per cent (44.03 per cent and 63 deputies per es.wikipedia's article on the election, 43.5 per cent in its article on the government) against the opposition CODE's 55.70 per cent and 87 deputies. The often-quoted 43.4 per cent sits at the low end of the range.

stops.stop: Valparaiso, the fleet comes back at dawn
stops.date_confidence: Attested: the fleet, which had sailed for joint exercises, reappeared off Valparaiso around dawn and the navy seized the port and city before the other services moved (es.wikipedia, 'Golpe de Estado en Chile de 1973').

stops.stop: Palacio de La Moneda, Radio Magallanes
stops.date_confidence: Attested: the final address went out over Radio Magallanes at about 10:15 a.m., the last station still transmitting; the tank and artillery assault on the palace began about 10:30 and the Hawker Hunters struck between about 11:30 a.m. and 12:08 p.m. (es.wikipedia). The English text quoted is Yoshie Furuhashi's translation, held by the Marxists Internet Archive.

stops.stop: Palacio de La Moneda, the Salon Independencia
stops.date_confidence: Attested by en.wikipedia's 'Death of Salvador Allende': at about 1:50 p.m. he ordered the defenders to surrender, shook hands with them in a line, then walked to the Salon Independencia; the physician Patricio Guijon turned back and saw him shoot himself. The body reached the Hospital Militar at about 17:30. The 2011 forensic panel found the injuries consistent with suicide by a rifle set to automatic fire.

stops.stop: Cementerio Santa Ines, Viña del Mar, the grave with another family's name
stops.date_confidence: Attested by es.wikipedia's 'Fundacion Salvador Allende': buried on 12 September 1973, clandestinely, in the tomb of the Grove family at the Cementerio de Santa Ines, Viña del Mar. Coordinates from Nominatim for the cemetery. The Nixon telephone transcript is National Security Archive EBB No. 437, Document 7, read as page images; the wording follows the scan, including the trailing 'though'.

stops.stop: Cementerio General, Santiago, the funeral held seventeen years late
stops.date_confidence: Attested by es.wikipedia's 'Fundacion Salvador Allende': the final obsequies were held on 4 September 1990 and the Mausoleo Salvador Allende was created at the Cementerio General de Santiago, the date chosen because it was the traditional Chilean presidential polling day. Coordinates are an approximate placement near the southern part of the cemetery, not a verified plot.

stops.stop: Cementerio General, Santiago, the exhumation
stops.date_confidence: Attested for the year and the finding: a court ordered the exhumation in May 2011, a Chilean television report on 31 May 2011 revealed a 300-page secret military account and two forensic experts initially suggested assassination, and in July 2011 the international panel concluded death by self-inflicted gunshot from a rifle set to automatic fire. The exact day of the exhumation was not confirmed and the stop is dated to the July finding.
